claims.claim: A geographer studies religion descriptively as a spatial and cultural phenomenon (distribution, diffusion, landscape imprint) and does not evaluate the truth of any tradition or rank traditions.

A universalizing religion seeks converts and is open in principle to all peoples (e.g., Christianity, Islam, Buddhism); an ethnic religion is associated with a particular people or place and generally does not proselytize (e.g., Hinduism, Judaism).

Religions diffuse from a hearth; the hearths of the largest universalizing religions are in Asia (Christianity and Islam in Southwest Asia / the eastern Mediterranean; Buddhism in South Asia near the India-Nepal border).

Religion diffuses through expansion diffusion (including contagious diffusion via proselytizing and hierarchical diffusion via conversion of a ruler/elite) and through relocation diffusion (believers migrating and re-establishing the faith).
Sacred spaces are places associated with a sense of the divine; religion imprints the cultural landscape through worship sites, sacred sites, burial/cemeteries, and religious calendars.
For 2020, Pew Research Center estimated Christians at about 2.3 billion, roughly 28.8% of world population (largest group).
For 2020, Pew estimated Muslims at about 25.6% of world population, and Muslims were the fastest-growing group over 2010-2020.
For 2020, Pew estimated the religiously unaffiliated ('nones') at about 1.9 billion, roughly 24.2% of world population, the third-largest category.

For 2020, Pew estimated Hindus at about 14.9%, Buddhists at about 4.1%, Jews at about 0.2%, and other religions at about 2.2% of world population; the analysis drew on more than 2,700 sources of data.

Secular denotes a separation between the state and religion; secularization refers to the weakening of religion's public influence; the religiously unaffiliated are a descriptive category of people who do not identify with any religion, not a religion.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Exact adherent counts and shares vary across sources and years and are estimates.
positions: Pew Research Center 2020 estimates used here
Other datasets (e.g., World Religion Database, national censuses) give slightly different figures
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Use a single authoritative, clearly dated source (Pew, 2020) and attribute it explicitly; present figures as rounded estimates, never as fixed exact totals.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft treated 'religion' as a generic study-skills placeholder ('a concept students use to organize information') with no geographic content, no distribution data, and no distinction between universalizing and ethnic religions. None of its substantive framing was usable.

sourceRecords.title: How the Global Religious Landscape Changed From 2010 to 2020
sourceRecords.notes: Report released June 9, 2025, describing 2020 global religious composition based on more than 2,700 sources of data. Figures verified from the report PDF via local text extraction: Christians about 2.3 billion / 28.8% (largest); Muslims about 25.6% and fastest-growing 2010-2020 (grew by 347 million); religiously unaffiliated about 1.9 billion / 24.2% (third-largest); Hindus 14.9%; Buddhists 4.1%; Jews about 0.2%; other religions about 2.2%. 'Other religions' category includes Baha'is, Daoists, Jains, Shintoists, Sikhs, Wiccans, Zoroastrians and folk/traditional religions. Copyrighted; used as dated, attributed figures only; no prose reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: Introduction to Human Geography, Chapter 6: Religion (incl. 6.3 Diffusion and 6.6 Key Terms)
sourceRecords.provider: David Dorrell & Joseph P. Henderson, University of North Georgia Press (via Social Sci LibreTexts)
sourceRecords.notes: CC BY 4.0 open textbook. Read chapter 6 landing page, 6.3 (Diffusion of Major Religions), and 6.6 (Key Terms Defined). Supports: universalizing religion = 'a religion that seeks converts'; ethnic religion = 'a religion associated with a particular ethnic group'; sacred spaces = 'places associated with a sense of the divine'; monotheism/polytheism; syncretic religion; secular = 'a condition of separation between a state and any religion'; hearths (Christianity/Islam eastern Mediterranean-Southwest Asia; Buddhism near the Nepalese-Indian border); diffusion types (hierarchical via conversion of a leader; relocation via missionary/migration; contagious via direct proselytizing). Prose written independently; only short term definitions recast in original wording.

sourceRecords.title: Introduction to Geography, 2.4: Geography of Religion
sourceRecords.provider: Cameron McCormick, Spokane Falls Community College (Open Washington, via Geosciences LibreTexts)
sourceRecords.notes: CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial) open textbook. Corroborates the universalizing/ethnic distinction: 'Universalizing religions breaks from bounds of place and ethnicity to seek converts' (examples Christianity, Islam, Buddhism); 'Ethnic religions are those that do not proselytize and are associated with a specific place or ethnic group' (examples Judaism, Hinduism); religions diffuse through migration, contact conversion, and organized missions. Treated as REFERENCE_ONLY given the NC restriction; facts synthesized, no wording reproduced.
